source.title: When Do Attention Circuits Form? Developmental Trajectories of Capability and Attention-Sink Emergence Across Three 1B-ClassArchitectures

page_placements.theme: Induction circuit composition in pretrained full transformers (upstream previous-token, duplicate-token and context heads)
Developmental order: induction heads relative to other circuits and abilities

record.file_problem: The text appears complete through the conclusion and references; no garbling or cutoff noted.
record.tranche_reason: The study tracks induction-circuit emergence and argues that, in DCLM-trained models, it is distinct in timing from BOS-attractor emergence; it also refines the phase-transition account with evidence of circuit turnover.
record.gate_note: The study reports induction-selectivity milestones, BOS-class fractions over training, circuit-recall results, and causal group-ablation outcomes. It does not measure the training-loss bump or loss falling with token index. PR measurements are not included as rows because PR itself is not a measure named in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Tracks induction-head formation across 10 checkpoints in three 1B-class models (Pythia 1B, OLMo 1B, OLMoE 1B-7B). This bears on V4 (induction heads appear in every run) and on V2/V7 (formation timing and head turnover). The authors argue the 'form at the transition and persist' account needs restating because circuit membership turns over. Their headline 'two transitions' result contrasts induction with attention-sink formation. Sinks are not part of induction formation, so that result is not evidence on V2 or V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right, with three qualifications. The 10–20× induction-before-sink gap holds only for the DCLM models; in Pythia the two co-emerge at ~6B, which the authors call a grid-resolution limit. The authors also conclude the induction function is installed early and stays stable while the heads carrying it turn over. Finally, the selectivity screen under-identifies the causal circuit because it misses duplicate-token heads.
record.recipe_differences: Uses per-head participation ratio, a capability-specific selectivity screen and group ablation on intermediate checkpoints; the cited original induction work used integrated-gradients-style attribution on small decoder-only models. This study uses 1B-class pretrained models and synthetic induction batches.
record.method_sensitivity: Observed emergence timing and curve shape vary across the tested model runs; the authors note checkpoint-grid resolution and different earliest published checkpoints. Pythia early-checkpoint evaluation uses fp32, while OLMo and OLMoE use fp16.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention-sink (BOS) head formation is a separate, later process: BOS-50% at 264B (OLMo) and 419B (OLMoE) versus induction at 23B and 20B. It is sharp in OLMo and gradual in Pythia and OLMoE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In 1B-class LMs, attention-sink formation is a distinct transition from, and later than, induction-head formation.

fits_no_version.finding: Duplicate-token heads, including one never induction-selective (L3·H15), are causally needed for synthetic induction in OLMoE. Ex-induction heads that become sinks are causally inert.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In large models, induction relies on duplicate-token heads as well as induction heads; selectivity screens under-identify the causal circuit.

record.problems: One training run per 1B-class model; only 10 sampled revisions per model (8 for OLMoE); checkpoint availability limits early trajectories; synthetic induction selectivity is not validated at every revision on natural text; no training-loss bump or in-context-learning loss-by-token-index analysis.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional per-layer BOS head counts (Tables 2–3), per-revision null-selectivity calibration, extensive per-head selectivity trajectories (Figure 3), and other capability-class turnover results. These were left out because they do not add a distinct result for the listed claim versions beyond the BOS trajectory, induction milestone, recall and causal-ablation rows retained here.

untested.parts: All of it: no small attention-only models, and no test of composition with a previous-token head.
Abruptness within a narrow window (grid too coarse), coincidence with an in-context-learning gain, and the loss-curve bump.
Other sizes, repeated seeds, other architectures beyond dense/MoE transformers, other modalities.
All of it. Timing differences across runs are confounded with corpus, architecture and earliest-checkpoint availability, and no ICL persistence is measured.
Mechanistic sub-steps inside individual head formation (e.g. previous-token then induction) at fine checkpoint resolution.

missing.what: Per-revision trajectory of the top Pythia induction head L4·H4: selectivity 3.9× at 1.07B, 171.8× at 6.3B. Bears on how abrupt formation is.
Formation-vs-final circuit Jaccard 0.33/0.33/0.29, stable at 0.2–0.5 across 30–100× thresholds. Strong early heads decay out (OLMoE L7·H15 165×→3×, L6·H1 156×→1×; Pythia L5·H7).
Formation-revision ablation effects omitted from rows: Pythia decay-out group −10.2pp, OLMoE late-joiners −1.7pp.

record.verdict_notes: Row r28 swaps Table 8 columns: final-checkpoint effect is −3.8pp, z = −2.9. Synthetic-induction top-1 baseline at the final checkpoint is only ~4–5%, so ablation effects are small in absolute terms. Each model is a single run and the checkpoint grid is coarse; OLMo and OLMoE earliest checkpoints are 2B and 20B tokens, so their induction timings are upper bounds and cannot support V5. The 'two transitions' headline concerns induction versus attention sinks, which is outside V2/V7 as stated. In OLMo, the previous-token milestone (≥30 heads at ≥30×, 117B) comes after the induction milestone (23B). This is threshold-dependent and not a V1 test.

versions.untested_parts: The causal tests concern synthetic induction and duplicate-token heads; the study does not directly test composition with a previous-token head or use small attention-only transformers.
The study measures induction-circuit formation across checkpoints but does not measure an in-context-learning loss gain, a training-loss bump, or their coincidence with induction formation.
No large-transformer in-context-learning loss-by-token-index measure or estimate of how much ICL induction heads carry.
Tests three specific 1B-class runs across two architecture families and two corpora; does not test other sizes, repeated training runs, other architectures or modalities.
Compares induction timing across three runs, but does not isolate corpus effects on induction timing or test whether ICL persists under different data or training setups.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare its carriers with induction heads.
Tests separation between induction-circuit and BOS-attractor emergence; does not resolve whether induction formation itself comprises internal sub-steps.
